lastCompletedStory.title: CRITICAL: isSidecarArgv over-matches and makes `cam stop` SIGTERM unrelated processes

openQuestions: scripts/cam/prd.json was already modified in the working tree (not committed) when this story started: it carries US-R1-001..004 (round-1 review findings filed as follow-up stories) plus a `review` block. This implementer intentionally left prd.json untouched/uncommitted per 'do not edit prd.json', on the assumption the supervisor's finalize step commits it (flips US-R1-001 passes:true and persists the already-present US-R1-002/003/004 entries). If the finalize step does NOT pick up an already-dirty prd.json from a prior interrupted session, that needs a harness-level look (not an implementer fix).
nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 fixed the CRITICAL over-match in `isSidecarArgv` (src/commands/stop.ts): it now additionally requires `argv[0]` to start with `/` (an absolute path), which real self-spawn argv always has (both production shapes are built from `resolveSelfInvokeArgv`, which spreads `process.execPath`, verified empirically absolute even under a relative invoke). This closes the false-positive class (`tail -F sidecar`, `rg sidecar`, `git log sidecar`) that got SIGTERM'd by the `cam stop` fallback scoped scan. Existing fixtures in test/commands/stop-name-agnostic.test.ts and test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts were updated to use absolute argv[0] paths (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/bin/bun`, `/usr/local/bin/cam`) since a bare `'bun'`/`'cam'` literal no longer matches under the new predicate; a new regression test/describe block in test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts asserts the tail/rg false-positive class is NOT matched. Three more round-1 review findings are already staged as prd.json stories (uncommitted, see openQuestions) for whichever agent picks them up next: US-R1-002 (WARNING, priority 2) — the same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose absolute execPath contains a space, because defaultListProcesses splits the raw `ps` args column on `/\s+/` and isSidecarArgv requires an exact 2-or-3 token count; fix needs to anchor on the last token + an absolute-path prefix rather than exact token count, tolerating spaces in argv[0]/argv[1]. US-R1-003 (WARNING, priority 3) — US-004's coverage never exercises the real `defaultListProcesses` (real `ps`+`lsof` parsing), only the pure `matchesSidecarForProject` fixture path; needs a real-process integration test (spawn a real process with the interpreted self-spawn argv shape in a temp cwd, assert discovery finds it and an adjacent non-sidecar command in the same cwd is NOT matched). US-R1-004 (WARNING, priority 4) — a patterns.md bullet is marked `[resolved 2026-08-02]` (full-date form) but the archiver's RESOLVED_MARKER_RE only matches `[resolved YYYY-MM]`; needs the marker fixed to `[resolved 2026-08]`, or reconsidered as still-live (it documents the LIVE isSidecarArgv shape contract, not a closed GOTCHA) rather than archived. GOTCHA for whichever story next touches this file: isSidecarArgv's token-count assumption (2 or 3 elements) is the exact thing US-R1-002 must relax — do not assume it still holds once that story lands.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Bun's Bun.spawn docs page does not document argv[0]/process.execPath absolute-path resolution explicitly, so the fix's core assumption (process.execPath is always an absolute path, even under a relative invoke) was instead verified empirically via `bun -e 'console.log(process.execPath)'` from a tmpdir, which confirmed an absolute filesystem path. The assumption held; no code change was needed.
